scope: Targeted independent review of the canonical guide at the named baseline, not a claim to have manually verified every historical edition.

sources.label: Repository: archive scan implementation
sources.quote: The archived repository scan is a rule-based search; matching patterns alone do not establish legal accuracy for every line.

items.title: Willful FBAR penalty ceiling
items.observed: The baseline summary presents the inflation-adjusted fixed amount as the willful maximum; the existing flag says the larger-of alternative was not independently opened.
items.finding: The statute also provides a 50% alternative, where greater; the fixed amount is not necessarily the overall ceiling. Penalties are conditional, not transfer fees.
items.action: Correct the ceiling and link both the statute and the current inflation-adjustment table; keep individual exposure blank.

items.title: A partial Wise quote is compared as fully priced
items.observed: The baseline comparison labels a cheapest fully priced option even though Wise rows say recipient-bank fees are not included, while the BOC example includes a Chase receiving fee.
items.finding: The two scenarios do not establish equal scope or a personalized cheapest route. Eligibility, payment method and receiving charges remain unknown.
items.action: Show verified components and unknowns separately; avoid a definitive winner until both personalized quotes use the same assumptions.

items.title: BOC full-amount delivery and fee conversion assumptions
items.observed: The baseline scenario includes a fixed full-amount charge and converts the CNY charges to USD using the selling rate.
items.finding: BOC note 5 restricts that service to specified intermediary arrangements; note 1 describes the buy rate when fees are collected in equivalent foreign currency. A CNY-funded comparison needs a separately stated assumption.
items.action: State the assumed correspondent relationship and fee-funding currency; show unconfirmed applicability and extra charges as blank/flagged.

items.title: Gross benchmark versus net received
items.observed: The baseline ladder defines the input as CNY worth the stated USD amount at the midpoint, then deducts modeled costs.
items.finding: That target is not a guarantee that the same USD amount reaches the destination. BOC says its public board is indicative; the midpoint is an analytical benchmark rather than a published bank charge.
items.action: Label the target as benchmark principal and disclose the estimated net separately; do not claim the amount received without a verified quote.

items.title: Eligibility depends on the source of funds
items.observed: The baseline landing page introduces one passport-and-tax-record route broadly for the user's unknown account.
items.finding: The cited SAFE Q&A addresses lawful current-account income such as wages; it does not establish eligibility for every kind of property, corporate balance, inheritance or citizenship/residence history.
items.action: Describe the route as conditional on the bank's classification, source documentation and any applicable approvals; leave the user's eligibility unverified.

items.title: Splitting is prohibited when used to evade limits
items.observed: The baseline landing page says not to split the amount without the evasion qualification, while the Wise provider publishes per-transfer limits.
items.finding: PBOC article 7 targets splitting to evade limit supervision; the cited text is not a blanket prohibition of every multiple-transfer schedule.
items.action: Keep the prohibition on evasion and borrowed quotas, while saying any multiple-transfer plan requires provider and bank approval and must not evade controls.

items.title: US currency gain and foreign-tax credit are conditional
items.observed: A parallel correction qualified the guide's main tax wording, but some baseline summary language still emphasizes only previously untaxed underlying income.
items.finding: A separate US foreign-currency gain can require analysis; a credit is conditional and does not automatically remove US tax. This review does not calculate the user's tax.
items.action: Keep the qualified explanation consistent in the landing page, summary, downloadable summary and tax table; refer the case to qualified US and China advisers.

items.title: Penalty exposure is not a transfer price
items.observed: The baseline CSV stores three prohibited-route penalty scenarios in a column named total_cost_usd, although their status is penalty.
items.finding: The cited regulation describes distinct violation categories and conditional legal consequences; a maximum penalty is not an ordinary charge or guaranteed outcome.
items.action: Separate legal exposure from actual transfer-cost columns or clearly mark those rows so downstream users cannot rank them as prices.

items.title: Live quotes and historic snapshots
items.observed: The guide records a dated BOC snapshot and Wise comparison samples; the cited public endpoints return current data and can change.
items.finding: A dated snapshot can support an illustrative calculation but is not an executable rate or a verified historic quote once the live endpoint changes.
items.action: Keep timestamp and time zone beside every illustration, explain the source snapshot, and request contemporaneous binding quotes; do not invent current prices.

items.title: Foreign-currency cash exceptions
items.observed: Some baseline rows describe carrying over the stated threshold as unavailable in one trip.
items.finding: SAFE's notice says 'in principle' and also lists exceptional situations in which a permit may be requested; it does not imply an unconditional ban in every case.
items.action: State the ordinary rule and narrow exceptions accurately, without presenting cash as a means to bypass currency controls.

items.title: Automated scan is not line-by-line legal certification
items.observed: The archived-site review counts lines examined by a pattern scan and the verifier checks source-link presence and arithmetic.
items.finding: Neither a pattern match nor a registered link proves every archived claim is supported by an official source; the automated checks do not fetch or interpret legal texts.
items.action: Report the scan as a scoped machine search, identify what was actually re-read, and retain uncertainty for historical editions.

items.title: Missing US filing history
items.observed: The user has not supplied whether prior returns, FBARs or information returns were required or filed.
items.finding: The IRS offers procedures with specific eligibility requirements, including a non-willfulness certification. Their applicability cannot be decided from the available facts.
items.action: Obtain account histories and prior filings; consult a qualified professional before choosing any disclosure or remediation procedure.
